hints.title: Find the original centre and radius
hints.body: Sketch the diameter endpoints and mark their midpoint, the centre. Calculate its coordinates and distance to either endpoint; track later centre movements with arrows.
hints.recap: A diameter passes through the centre; its endpoints are twice a radius apart.
hints.pitfall: Do not use the whole diameter as the radius.
hints.pause: Record the centre and squared radius.

recall.reminder: A diameter passes through the centre; its endpoints are twice a radius apart.

hints.title: Move the centre in the stated order
hints.body: Apply the translation to the centre, then reflect it in the x-axis. Keep a separate record of what happens to the radius.
hints.recap: Apply successive transformations in the stated order.
hints.pitfall: Reflection in the x-axis changes the vertical coordinate.
hints.pause: Find the centre after these two moves.

recall.reminder: Apply successive transformations in the stated order.

hints.title: Enlarge about the new centre
hints.body: The enlargement is about the circle’s own centre, so it stays fixed. Apply the scale factor to the radius before squaring it.
hints.recap: An enlargement scales lengths by its stated factor.
hints.pitfall: The circle equation uses the square of the radius.
hints.pause: Build the final circle equation from your centre and new radius.

recall.reminder: An enlargement scales lengths by its stated factor.

solution:
The original centre is (3+72, 3+52)=(5, 4). Its squared radius is (5−3)2+(4−3)2=5.

The left translation sends the centre to (2, 4), and reflection in the x-axis sends it to (2, −4). These transformations preserve the radius. The enlargement is about this resulting centre, so it stays fixed while the radius becomes 45 and its square becomes 80.

The final equation is (x−2)2+(y+4)2=80, option D.
knowledgePattern: Track circle centre separately from radius through transformations
